title: uchar-ir-v1
description: Structural schema for the 'uchar-ir-v1' format in its L3 shape (spec/proposals/V1-WIREMIGRATIE.md, section 7, landings L1, L2 and L3): the former 'regelspraak-ir-v0' dump of the reference frontend's fully resolved model with its CONTAINER restructured (L1), its REFERENCE LAYER reduced to the symbolic form (L2) and its TYPE SYSTEM in the v1 nodes (L3), and nothing else. The root nests {format, model, rules, diagnostics} (decision V3 (b)): 'model' is the declaration set of IR-SPEC ch. 2, as lists in declaration order (WF-019), with no map keys; 'rules' carries the resolved rule lists under their v0 keys, in v0 order; 'diagnostics' is the producer's own account (WF-113). An ObjectType carries its members as Attribute and Characteristic nodes with their own facets (TimelineFacet), and a Domain wraps a name and a datatype that carries no self-name at the declaration position (domainDatatype). A reference carries only its symbolic form (L2): the five reference classes carry no type annotation, because the declaration is the one source; an attribute reference names its navigation by role bindings alone; the range of an instance fold, a quantifier fold and an allocation is written, never derived; one RoleMembership node names the fact type and the role the subject fills; a fact creation and a scoped uniqueness carry their symbolic fields alone; and the datatype union has no member for an unknown type (B16). The type system is the v1 one (L3): a number is a Number, and a percentage a Number with the unit '%' that carries the presentation tag 'percentage' at a declaration (B14); a date is one Date node with its precision (B15); a unit is a Unit whose conversion factor is an exact rational {num, den} (B17 (i)) and whose declaration carries its spellings; a unit system is a list of units; a day kind is a DayKind node with its plural; and a parameter carries the attribute's timeline facet without a timeline name (B18). Every other node keeps its v0 name, field spellings and enum values until its own landing. Canonical key order is the 'properties' order of this schema: the migration script and every emitter write exactly that order, and every node L1 left untouched keeps the order its v0 emitter wrote, less the keys L2 removed. Every object is closed (additionalProperties:false) and lists every always-emitted key as required; node subtypes are discriminated on the 'node' field. Exception, by the decided wire-entry discipline (IR-SPEC, Method): extension fields carrying v1 deltas (verbindendeRol on an object creation, bronRol, bronPad, and bronAnnotaties — of these, bronPad is the multi-step fold-source range of IR-SPEC ch. 4.3 / WF-102, two or more RolBindings subject-outwards and mutually exclusive with bronRol, which is the one-step spelling of the same field; and bronAnnotaties carries the statute annotations on a resolved rule, when present a non-empty list of non-empty strings and absent otherwise) are optional where L2 makes none of them required (the allocation's verbindendeRol and the range of a fold and of a quantifier fold, under the conditions stated on those nodes), the datatype union admits the extension nodes SumType (the payload-carrying variant family, CONSTRUCTS row 36), ListType (the sequence type, CONSTRUCTS row 10) and StructType (the record datatype, spec/proposals/PHASE5C-TUTORIAL.md §2), the expr union admits the extension nodes TemporalRead, Construct, Match, BinderRef, StructLiteral, FieldAccess, the row-10 fold family (ListLiteral, Lambda, IfThenElse, Invoke, Fold, MapList, FilterList, ListLength) and the value-level binding Let (spec/proposals/PHASE5C-TUTORIAL.md §6), and the optional lists functionDefs (under 'model') and prioritizedDefaults (under 'rules') carry the named-logic and prioritized-defaults extensions, and a Default carries the optional excepties field — its nested exception groups (RUNTIME-SEMANTICS ch. 7.9) — the v0 emitter produces none of them EXCEPT Let and BinderRef, which the RegelSpraak frontend has emitted for a §13.4.2.10 variabelendeel since the let-lowering card (2026-09-01); when present they are all written whole, never null. Wire epoch v0.10 (the rename epoch, 2026-08-29): the prioritized-defaults spellings (prioritizedDefaults/Default/ExceptionGroup and the defaults list) are the only valid ones; a file in the pre-rename spelling (see the formerly notes, IR-SPEC ch. 6.1 and RUNTIME-SEMANTICS ch. 7.1) fails loudly against the closed objects. Section citations (e.g. §13.3.3) point into the source language spec by number only.

model.description: The model layer: the declaration set of IR-SPEC ch. 2. The six former v0 registries are lists in declaration order, each entry carrying its name on its node (there is no map key); timelines are unchanged from v0; the day kinds are a list of DayKind nodes, each carrying its own spellings (L3). functionDefs is an extension list: optional, written whole or not at all.

functionDefs.description: Extension list (v1, CONSTRUCTS row 10): named reusable logic (FunctionDef) per spec/IR-SPEC.md ch. 2.11. Optional; the v0 emitter never produces it.

rules.description: The rule layer: the v0 resolved rule lists under their v0 keys and in v0 order, their content unchanged until their own M step. prioritizedDefaults is an extension list: optional, written whole or not at all.

prioritizedDefaults.description: Extension list (v1, Phase 4): prioritized-defaults groups (characteristic and attribute forms) per spec/RUNTIME-SEMANTICS.md ch. 7. Optional; the v0 emitter never produces it.

Number.description: A number (IR-SPEC ch. 2.4). 'whole' and 'decimals' carry the precision form; which combinations are well-formed is WF-007, a verifier check, so the schema admits any integer for 'decimals'. 'sign' is always written and keeps its v0 enum spelling until its own landing; a number declared without a sign is ONBEPAALD. 'unit' absent: the number carries no unit. A percentage is a Number whose unit is '%' (or a rate with '%' as its numerator), delta B14 of spec/proposals/V1-WIREMIGRATIE.md and CONSTRUCTS row 27; 'presentation' is its dialect(regelspraak) presentation tag, the one value 'percentage', written only at a declaration position (the datatype of an attribute, a parameter or a domain, a sum-type payload, a list element, a struct field, a function or lambda parameter, a function result) and never on a type annotation, where the verifier refuses it (WF-007). The tag carries no meaning for evaluation. Key order is this 'properties' order.

Date.description: A date (IR-SPEC ch. 2.4; delta B15 of spec/proposals/V1-WIREMIGRATIE.md): one node, parameterised by its precision. 'day' and 'millisecond' share no order (WF-036), so the precision is always written.

SumType.description: Extension node (IR-SPEC Method; wire node SumType, never emitter-produced): the payload-carrying variant family of CONSTRUCTS row 36 — a declared, nominal sum type, declared as a Domain in 'model.domains' (there without its 'domain' self-name: DomainSumType) and repeated whole at every use site. Each constructor carries a 'name' and either one 'payload' datatype (unary) or null (nullary). See spec/IR-SPEC.md ch. 2.4 (WF-060/061).

ListType.description: Extension node (IR-SPEC Method; wire node ListType, never emitter-produced): an ordered, possibly empty sequence type of CONSTRUCTS row 10. 'element' is the single element datatype (first-order and non-list — WF-065). See spec/IR-SPEC.md ch. 2.4 (WF-065).

StructType.description: Extension node (IR-SPEC Method; wire node StructType, never emitter-produced): the record datatype of the Phase-5c core (spec/proposals/PHASE5C-TUTORIAL.md §2) — a declared, nominal record, declared as a Domain in 'model.domains' (there without its 'domain' self-name: DomainStructType) and repeated whole at every use site, exactly the SumType/ListType landing pattern. Each field carries a 'name' and a non-null 'datatype' (a number, day-precision date, sum type or struct type — WF-071). See spec/IR-SPEC.md ch. 2.4 (WF-071/072).

domainDatatype.description: The datatype at the DECLARATION position, Domain.datatype (IR-SPEC ch. 2.3). It admits the same datatype nodes as 'datatype', except that Enumeratie, SumType and StructType appear here in a form without their self-name field ('domein' on Enumeratie, 'domain' on SumType and StructType): the Domain wrapper carries the name, and a second spelling of it cannot be written. At every REFERENCE position (attributes, parameters, expressions, payloads, fields, elements) the 'datatype' union applies unchanged: there that field is the domain reference of IR-SPEC ch. 2.4 (WF-003), not a self-name, and stays required. The three declaration forms share their remaining field schemas with the reference forms by JSON pointer, so each field is defined once.

DomainEnumeratie.description: Enumeratie at the declaration position of a Domain: the 'domein' self-name is absent (see domainDatatype); 'waarden' is the reference form's own field schema.

DomainSumType.description: SumType at the declaration position of a Domain: the 'domain' self-name is absent (see domainDatatype); 'constructors' is the reference form's own field schema.

DomainStructType.description: StructType at the declaration position of a Domain: the 'domain' self-name is absent (see domainDatatype); 'fields' is the reference form's own field schema.

Unit.description: A unit where it occurs (IR-SPEC ch. 2.5): on a Number, and as the denominator of a rate. 'abbreviation' is its primary spelling. 'system' names the declaring UnitSystem (WF-034 (r)); it is absent for the built-in '%' and for the bare calendar units. 'canonical' and 'factorToCanonical' are the conversion pair, both present or both absent (WF-092). The factor is an exact positive rational, how many canonical units equal one of this unit, written {num, den} without a node discriminator (delta B17 (i) of spec/proposals/V1-WIREMIGRATIE.md, CONSTRUCTS row 26); that it is in lowest terms is a verifier check (WF-092), because a schema cannot state a greatest common divisor. 'denominator' is the denominator unit of a rate. No field is ever null: absent is the one spelling of a field not given. A unit's further spellings belong to its declaration (DeclaredUnit), so an occurrence cannot carry them. Key order is this 'properties' order.

DeclaredUnit.description: A unit as its UnitSystem declares it (IR-SPEC ch. 2.5): the node of Unit, and after its fields 'spellings', the further spellings that resolve to this unit (word and plural aliases), at least one when present. Only the declaration carries them: an occurrence of the unit is a Unit, which has no such field, so a spelling written there cannot be accepted and dropped. The other fields are Unit's own field schemas, by JSON pointer, so each is defined once. Key order is this 'properties' order.

Functie.description: A builtin or an aggregation (IR-SPEC ch. 4.3/4.6). The RANGE of an instance fold is written, never derived (delta B12 of spec/proposals/V1-WIREMIGRATIE.md; CONSTRUCTS row 4): with an elementObjecttype, exactly one argument and a kind other than TOTAAL, exactly one of bronRol (the one-step range) and bronPad (the multi-step range, WF-102) is present. A TOTAAL without either is the subject's own read over its own attribute (the verifier holds that it is, WF-083), and no fold carries both. With two or more arguments the node is the listed value fold, whose operands are ordinary reads: it has no range, whatever elementObjecttype it carries.

navigatieBindingen.description: The navigation hops as symbolic role bindings, subject-outward, one binding per hop — the bound role is the role the hop reaches (the far role). Present exactly when the reference reads off the subject: a reference without it is the subject's own read, whose objecttype is the subject type (WF-053); the zero-hop self-reference of IR-SPEC ch. 4.1a is such a read. Written whole or not at all, never null.

ExprOnopgelost.description: An expression the resolver could not resolve; surfaces as an explicit marker. 'type' is optional: absent means the type is unknown, present it is a real datatype, never null.

TemporalRead.description: Extension node (v1, CONSTRUCTS row 11): the point-in-time read read(tl, d) of spec/RUNTIME-SEMANTICS.md ch. 3.3. Never emitter-produced; basis, datum and type are required and non-null.

Construct.description: Extension node (IR-SPEC Method; wire node Construct, never emitter-produced): builds a sum-type constructor value (CONSTRUCTS row 36; spec/RUNTIME-SEMANTICS.md ch. 9.1). 'argument' is an expr iff the constructor is unary, null for a nullary constructor. 'type' (the SumType) is required and non-null.

Match.description: Extension node (IR-SPEC Method; wire node Match, never emitter-produced): deconstructs a sum-type value, one arm per declared constructor (CONSTRUCTS row 36; spec/RUNTIME-SEMANTICS.md ch. 9.2). A unary arm carries a 'binder' name, a nullary arm carries null. 'type' (the result datatype) and 'scrutinee' are required and non-null.

BinderRef.description: Extension node (IR-SPEC Method; wire node BinderRef, EMITTER-PRODUCED since the let-lowering card, 2026-09-01): reads the nearest enclosing binder of its name — a match arm's, a lambda/function parameter, or a Let binder (CONSTRUCTS rows 36 and 24; spec/RUNTIME-SEMANTICS.md ch. 9.2 / ch. 10.6). The RegelSpraak emitter produces one for every read of a §13.4.2.10 variabele in a rule's result part. Deliberately distinct from VariabeleRef, which since that card survives only as the residual marker for a variable the resolver could NOT bind (row 24). 'name' is required and non-null; the read carries no type of its own, the binder's declaration is the one source (B13).

StructLiteral.description: Extension node (IR-SPEC Method; wire node StructLiteral, never emitter-produced): builds a record value (spec/proposals/PHASE5C-TUTORIAL.md §2; spec/RUNTIME-SEMANTICS.md ch. 11). 'fields' supplies exactly the declared fields, each once, in declaration order — WF-073; a field whose value evaluates leeg propagates (the whole literal is leeg, the no-hole rule). 'type' (the StructType) is required and non-null.

FieldAccess.description: Extension node (IR-SPEC Method; wire node FieldAccess, never emitter-produced): reads one declared field of a record (spec/proposals/PHASE5C-TUTORIAL.md §2; spec/RUNTIME-SEMANTICS.md ch. 11). 'base' is struct-typed and 'field' is one of its declared fields; the node 'type' is that field's datatype — WF-074. A leeg base propagates. 'type' and 'base' are required and non-null.

Lambda.description: Extension node (IR-SPEC Method; wire node Lambda, never emitter-produced): a typed anonymous function (CONSTRUCTS row 10; spec/RUNTIME-SEMANTICS.md ch. 10). Position-restricted to the 'function' operand of Fold/MapList — WF-069 (not a schema concern); its 'body' is closed. Carries no 'type': a lambda is never a value.

ListLiteral.description: Extension node (IR-SPEC Method; wire node ListLiteral, never emitter-produced): an ordered list value (CONSTRUCTS row 10; spec/RUNTIME-SEMANTICS.md ch. 10.1). Every element carries the declared element datatype of 'type' (a ListType) — WF-066. 'type' is required and non-null.

IfThenElse.description: Extension node (IR-SPEC Method; wire node IfThenElse, never emitter-produced): a value-level conditional (CONSTRUCTS row 10; spec/RUNTIME-SEMANTICS.md ch. 10.2). Position-restricted to lambda and function bodies — WF-069 (not a schema concern); the guard reuses the condition union; both branches agree on 'type'. 'type', 'condition', 'then' and 'else' are required and non-null.

Invoke.description: Extension node (IR-SPEC Method; wire node Invoke, never emitter-produced): calls a FunctionDef by name (CONSTRUCTS row 10; spec/RUNTIME-SEMANTICS.md ch. 10.2). Arity, argument and result typing: WF-068. 'type' is required and non-null.

Fold.description: Extension node (IR-SPEC Method; wire node Fold, never emitter-produced): the left fold (CONSTRUCTS row 10; spec/RUNTIME-SEMANTICS.md ch. 10.2). 'function' is a two-parameter (accumulator, element) Lambda; a bare FunctionDef name is structurally valid on the wire but WF-069 requires the inline Lambda (a named function reaches a fold through a lambda body that Invokes it). The accumulator/init/body/type share one first-order non-list datatype — WF-070. 'type', 'list' and 'init' are required and non-null.

MapList.description: Extension node (IR-SPEC Method; wire node MapList, never emitter-produced): the order-preserving map (CONSTRUCTS row 10; spec/RUNTIME-SEMANTICS.md ch. 10.2). 'function' is a one-parameter Lambda; a bare FunctionDef name is structurally valid on the wire but WF-069 requires the inline Lambda (a named function reaches a map through a lambda body that Invokes it). 'type' (a ListType) is the ListType of the body's datatype — WF-070. 'type' and 'list' are required and non-null.

FilterList.description: Extension node (IR-SPEC Method; wire node FilterList, never emitter-produced): keeps the elements whose 'condition' holds with 'binder' bound to the element (CONSTRUCTS row 10; spec/RUNTIME-SEMANTICS.md ch. 10.2) — the aggregation-filter precedent (a binder plus a condition, never a boolean-bodied lambda). 'type' (the source ListType) equals the source's type — WF-070. 'type', 'list' and 'condition' are required and non-null.

ListLength.description: Extension node (IR-SPEC Method; wire node ListLength, never emitter-produced): the element count (CONSTRUCTS row 10; spec/RUNTIME-SEMANTICS.md ch. 10.2). 'type' is a whole Number — WF-070. 'type' and 'list' are required and non-null.

Let.description: Extension node (IR-SPEC Method; wire node Let, EMITTER-PRODUCED since the let-lowering card, 2026-09-01): the value-level binding (spec/proposals/PHASE5C-TUTORIAL.md §6, question 2 = A; spec/RUNTIME-SEMANTICS.md ch. 10.6). The RegelSpraak frontend lowers a §13.4.2.10 variabelendeel ('Daarbij geldt: ...') to one Let per declared variable that the rule's RESULT part reads, nested in declaration order (§11.1 rule 1, first-declared outermost); a variable read only in the voorwaarde is substituted at its use site instead, because no expr node can span the separate 'voorwaarde' and 'waarde' wire fields of a resolved rule. 'binder' is visible only in 'body', never in its own 'value' — WF-076; it joins the WF-064 binder regime. The node 'type' equals the 'body' type — WF-076. Call-by-need (maintainer decision O3, 2026-09-01): the 'value' is evaluated in the enclosing scope at the FIRST read of the binder and reused for every further read; a read whose 'value' evaluates leeg makes the WHOLE Let leeg (the leeg-barrier, at the read place), so a body binder is never leeg — which is what carries the WF-069 widening (IfThenElse becomes admissible inside Let bodies) and the WF-077 condition-operand discipline; a binder the body never reads is never evaluated at all (no leeg, no fault, no channel fact) and the body's outcome is the Let's. 'type', 'binder', 'value' and 'body' are required and non-null.

InstanceSetBranch.description: Extension node (IR-SPEC Method; wire node InstanceSetBranch): one selection of an InstanceSetUnion — an element type, the one-step relation the selection ranges over, and an optional die/dat subselection evaluated PER CONTRIBUTOR. 'elementType' is carried nullable so a missing one is a WF-110 violation the verifier REPORTS with its rule, never a load failure; 'sourceRole' is required and non-null, because the selection's relation is written and nothing derives it (B12). There is deliberately no path spelling here: the multi-step range under a count is WF-102's and this node does not reopen it.

InstanceSetUnion.description: Extension node (IR-SPEC Method; wire node InstanceSetUnion, EMITTER-PRODUCED): the §5.7 concatenation of subject expressions as a set of INSTANCES — the source of an instance count (CONSTRUCTS row 1; spec/IR-SPEC.md ch. 4.3, semantics spec/RUNTIME-SEMANTICS.md ch. 3.4d). It carries no 'type': it denotes instances, not a value, so there is no annotation to twist and none to believe. Admissible ONLY as the single argument of an AANTAL aggregation, with at least two branches, and the count carrying it names no source of its own — WF-110. The members are the UNION of the branches' contributors, deduplicated on instance identity.

FunctionDef.description: Extension node (IR-SPEC Method; wire node FunctionDef, never emitter-produced): named reusable logic — DMN's Business Knowledge Model (CONSTRUCTS row 10; spec/IR-SPEC.md ch. 2.11). Carried by the optional 'functionDefs' list under 'model'. Ci-unique names, typed unique parameters, a resolvable 'result', a closed 'body', and an acyclic invocation graph: WF-067.

TekstReeksDeel.description: A part of a text sequence: a literal fragment or an interpolated expression.

navigatieBinding.description: The one navigation hop of a navigated characteristic check as a symbolic role binding — the bound role is the role the hop reaches, and the characteristic lives on the type it reaches. Absent: the check reads the subject itself (IR-SPEC ch. 4.1a and ch. 4.5). Written whole or not at all, never null.

RoleMembership.description: The role check (IR-SPEC ch. 4.5): true iff a link of the declared fact type 'factType' exists in which the subject fills 'role', named by its declared name, and whose other role is filled by an instance of 'counterpartType'; 'negated': no such link exists. 'counterpartType' is optional: absent, the other role's declared filler type is meant; present, it names a declared object type that is a subtype of, or equal to, the declared filler type of the other role (WF-034, IR-SPEC ch. 4.6 (o)); the migration and the emitter write the field only where it narrows (the L2 card, backlog/done/20260923-l2-referentielaag.md, U12). One node for both directions of the check (delta B9 of spec/proposals/V1-WIREMIGRATIE.md; CONSTRUCTS row 5); its key order is this 'properties' order.

kwantor.description: The quantifier over the instance range. ALLE = every contributor satisfies 'toets'; GEEN = none does; the three counting forms compare the NUMBER of contributors that satisfy it with 'drempel' (TEN_MINSTE: count >= drempel; TEN_HOOGSTE: count <= drempel; PRECIES: count == drempel). The vocabulary is Samengesteld's, over instances instead of parts. DE is NOT admitted here: the bare definite describes ONE member and is not a quantification over a set (WF-108 (a) refuses a hand-written one by name).

drempel.description: The counting quantifier's threshold — Samengesteld's field, under Samengesteld's rule (WF-041: at least 1). Written EXACTLY under TEN_MINSTE / TEN_HOOGSTE / PRECIES and omitted under ALLE / GEEN, which is where this node diverges from Samengesteld (there the field is always present and a zero nobody reads): a field that is meaningful in one position and inert everywhere else can say anything. The conditional below is the wire half of WF-108 (e); the verifier cites the rule.

elementObjecttype.description: The instance type quantified over — the POPULATION, extensionally (IR-SPEC ch. 2.2): the contributors are the instances the range reaches whose type is the subtype-or-equal of this one.

filter.description: The die/dat subselection, evaluated PER CONTRIBUTOR with the element as subject — the same field, the same reading and the same machinery as Functie.filter (RUNTIME-SEMANTICS ch. 3.4a). It selects WHICH members are quantified over; 'toets' is what each selected member must satisfy.

toets.description: The quantified matrix, evaluated PER CONTRIBUTOR with the element as subject. Nullable on the wire so a missing matrix is a citable WF-108 (d) violation rather than a load failure with no rule to name.

bronRol.description: Extension field (wire-entry discipline, IR-SPEC Method): the one-step range — the connecting relation with the role whose filler instances the quantifier RANGES OVER bound. Spelled exactly as Functie.bronRol. Exactly one of bronRol and bronPad is present: the range is written, never derived (B12). Never null.

bronPad.description: Extension field (wire-entry discipline, IR-SPEC Method): the MULTI-STEP range, the relations walked subject-outwards, each step spelled exactly as bronRol is. Two or more steps; the one-step range IS bronRol and the two fields are mutually exclusive (WF-108 (c), the WF-102 discipline under this node's own rule).

Kwantorvouw.description: Extension node (IR-SPEC Method; wire node Kwantorvouw): the QUANTIFIER FOLD — first-order quantification of a condition over the members of a linked instance set (IR-SPEC ch. 4.5; RUNTIME-SEMANTICS ch. 3.9a). The first-order sibling of Samengesteld, which quantifies over PARTS of one subject; this one quantifies over INSTANCES, and takes its range fields from the instance fold (ch. 4.3) unchanged.

ConditieOnopgelost.description: A condition the resolver could not resolve; surfaces as an explicit marker.

Geldigheid.description: A validity window; 'vanaf'/'tot' are strict ISO dates (four-two-two digit fields, digits only, no sign and no extended year — WF-084's date-literal grammar, IR-SPEC ch. 4.1) or null for open-ended. The pattern is load-bearing, not decoration: the verifier holds a bound as an OPAQUE STRING and orders it lexicographically for WF-021's overlap check (which states the assumption in as many words), and that ordering is sound only inside this lexeme. The interpreter and the ASP backend held bounds the same way until 2026-09-23; since then they read the evaluation date and both bounds through the strict date reader, compare day numbers and refuse a non-date naming its position. Measured 2026-09-11 without the pattern: '+012026-01-01' as a bound made the interpreter and the ASP backend apply a rule version that the Drools backend, which parses the lexeme, did not — one document, two answers — while 'niet-een-datum' passed every reader in the house. A pattern cannot check the calendar; '2026-02-30' matches here and is refused one field deeper, by WF-101 in the verifier and by each executor's date reader.

ObjectType.description: An object type (IR-SPEC ch. 2.2). Since M1 each attribute and characteristic is a node carrying its own facets; v0 carried those facets in eight side-maps keyed by member name, so a facet without a member can no longer be written. 'plural' absent = none declared.

supertype.description: The single direct parent, by declared name; absent = a root type. An extension field under the Method's discipline: optional, never required, never null, written whole or not at all. The type is a bare string and NOT an array on purpose (IR-SPEC ch. 2.2, WF-106): single parenthood holds by wire SHAPE, so a second direct parent is not a document the verifier rejects but one that cannot be written — this closed node refuses the array form here, which is where that refusal is enforced. The cost is stated rather than hidden: WF-106 therefore carries no verifier check and no corpus/negatief witness, and its witnesses live in the frontends that read the language above this wire.

Attribute.description: An attribute of an ObjectType (IR-SPEC ch. 2.2), in declaration order. 'plural' absent = none declared; 'dimensions' absent = scalar; when present it is non-empty (minItems 1, WF-004), so a scalar attribute has one spelling; 'timeline' absent = not time-dependent. 'datatype' admits null exactly as the v0 attribute map did: a datatype-less attribute is a loadable document, and the verifier refuses it (WF-059).

Characteristic.description: A characteristic of an ObjectType (IR-SPEC ch. 2.2), in declaration order. 'kind' is the presentation tag and is always written; a characteristic untagged in v0 is ZELFSTANDIG. The values keep their v0 spelling until M8. 'timeline' absent = not time-dependent.

TimelineFacet.description: The time-dependence of one member (IR-SPEC ch. 2.2). 'granularity' is required and non-null, so a facet without a grid cannot be written; the values keep their v0 spelling until M8. 'count' is always written (1 = single-period). That it is at least 1 is WF-005, a verifier check, so the schema admits any integer here. 'timelineName' is present iff the attribute was declared via a named timeline; a Characteristic's facet is CharacteristicTimelineFacet, which has no such field.

CharacteristicTimelineFacet.description: The TimelineFacet of a Characteristic (IR-SPEC ch. 2.2): the same node without 'timelineName'. v0 recorded no timeline name for a characteristic, so M1 keeps that position closed: an open one would be a wire field no producer writes and no reader checks. 'granularity' and 'count' are the attribute facet's own field schemas, by JSON pointer, so each is defined once.

ParameterTimelineFacet.description: The TimelineFacet of a Parameter (IR-SPEC ch. 2.10): the same node without 'timelineName', for the reason CharacteristicTimelineFacet states: no parameter records a timeline name, so an open position would be a wire field no producer writes and no reader checks. 'granularity' and 'count' are the attribute facet's own field schemas, by JSON pointer.

Domain.description: A named, reusable datatype (IR-SPEC ch. 2.3). The name is written once, here; the datatype at this declaration position carries no self-name (domainDatatype).

Parameter.description: A top-level named value (IR-SPEC ch. 2.10): its declared name, its datatype and, when it is time-dependent, its timeline facet (delta B18 of spec/proposals/V1-WIREMIGRATIE.md). The facet is ParameterTimelineFacet: no parameter records a timeline name, so the position is closed as a characteristic's is. Key order is this 'properties' order.

UnitSystem.description: A unit system (IR-SPEC ch. 2.5): its declared name and its units, as a list in declaration order. Each unit is written once, with its further spellings on the unit itself (Unit.spellings); there is no second map of spellings beside the units. Key order is this 'properties' order.

besluit.description: Characteristic defaults only: attribute (true) or do-not-attribute (false); null on attribute defaults.

voorwaarde.description: The justification; null only on the initialisation default (its justification is input-emptiness, ch. 7.3).

consequentie.description: Attribute defaults only: the default's value; a leeg-evaluating consequence falls through.

initialisatie.description: The initialisation default (lowest only): justified iff the target is empty in the input facts.

ongeordend.description: Declared-unordered (ch. 7.9): two or more exception groups require this marking, the root regime applied at every level; a differing-deciding exception group propagates the conflict to the root (WF-075).

excepties.description: Extension field (v1, Phase 5c): the nested exception groups of RUNTIME-SEMANTICS ch. 7.9 — a default's exception slot as a rose tree. A default carrying excepties is either a group-default (no own besluit/consequentie — its exception groups are its decision, carrying a multi-member base or exception group as a chain position) or a form-a default (own besluit/consequentie too — the exception groups decide first, its own consequence the fall-back when they decide nothing). The initialisation and input defaults are root-only. Never emitter-produced.

defaults.description: One exception group — a member of a Default's excepties: a default chain (descending, highest first) inheriting the root group's target, itself possibly nesting via Default.excepties. Carries no target of its own.

ExceptionGroup.description: Extension node (v1, Phase 5c): one exception group — a member of a Default's excepties (RUNTIME-SEMANTICS ch. 7.9). Never emitter-produced.

attribuut.description: Attribute-defaults target; a group carries exactly one of kenmerk/attribuut (WF-050).

ongeordend.description: Declared-unordered (ch. 7.2): multiple defaults groups on one target are admissible iff every one carries this marking; differing simultaneous decisions route to the §9.5 channel.

PrioritizedDefaults.description: Extension node (v1, Phase 4): the prioritized-defaults group — defaults in descending priority; the highest default that decides wins. Characteristic target: besluit (true = attribute, false = do-not-attribute); attribute target: consequentie (a leeg-evaluating consequence falls through); the initialisation default (lowest) is justified iff the target is empty in the input.

DayKind.description: A day kind (IR-SPEC ch. 2.9): its singular 'name' and its optional 'plural', the spelling it takes as a duration unit. These two are every spelling a day kind has on the wire; WF-017 holds them against the calendar spellings and against the other day kinds'. Key order is this 'properties' order.

verbindendeRol.description: Extension field (wire-entry discipline, IR-SPEC Method): the created-side role of the back-link, named explicitly — required where the type-pair derivation is role-ambiguous (a self-typed pair). Written whole or not at all, never null.

The recipient relation: the connecting fact type with the role the doelType instances fill bound. Required: the allocation's relation is written, never derived (delta B12 of spec/proposals/V1-WIREMIGRATIE.md; CONSTRUCTS row 4).

scopeRol.description: The scope-parent role of a parent-scoped uniqueness, named symbolically — the bound role is the role the scope hop reaches (its filler is the scope parent). Its presence IS the scoping: a uniqueness without it is unscoped (B8). Written whole or not at all, never null.

Diagnostic.description: The producer's own account of what stayed unresolved in a document it did write (WF-113). 'severity' is WARNING only: an ERROR means the producer refused to write the document, and INFO is not a wire severity. A 'message' that is neither empty nor blank, a 'line' of at least 0 (0 = no source position, a hand-built document) and the accounting of every Onopgelost node are verifier checks (WF-113), so 'line' admits any integer here.
